pack.name: Sustainability and Resource Efficiency
pack.description: Provider-neutral environmental sustainability and resource-efficiency screening — utilization assumptions, idle capacity, right-sizing, data retention/lifecycle, and proportional accelerator use. Does not fabricate carbon-emission percentages; thematic architecture guidance only.

rules.title: Utilization assumptions for continuously allocated capacity
rules.description: Continuously allocated compute/storage should state utilization assumptions or why always-on capacity is required. Do not invent carbon percentages.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document utilization assumptions or always-on justification in metadata.ChangeDescription; avoid numeric emissions claims without methodology.

rules.title: Idle-capacity and scheduling strategy
rules.description: Workloads with idle periods should describe scale-to-zero, scheduling, or accepted idle waste — distinct from pure cost optimization when environmental impact is in scope.

rules.title: Right-sizing and accelerator proportionality
rules.description: SKU/accelerator choices (including GPUs) should be proportional to stated need; oversized accelerators without justification are a resource-efficiency finding.
rules.remediationGuidance: Justify compute/accelerator sizing against workload assumptions in metadata.ChangeDescription and services[].Tags.

rules.title: Data retention and storage lifecycle discipline
rules.description: Retention and storage lifecycle should match business need; unbounded retention is a resource-efficiency and sustainability concern as well as a cost one.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document retention/lifecycle for datastores[] in governance.RequiredControls.

rules.title: Unnecessary replication and data movement minimized
rules.description: Cross-region replication and large data movement should be justified; defaulting to global copies without need wastes resources.
rules.remediationGuidance: Explain replication/data-movement necessity in relationships and governance.PolicyConstraints.

rules.title: Recomputation versus caching tradeoff considered
rules.description: Expensive recomputation loops (including AI inference context replay) should consider caching/batching where quality allows.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document recomputation vs caching/batching choices for heavy paths in metadata.ChangeDescription.

rules.title: Consumption observability for resource-heavy workloads
rules.description: Resource-heavy designs (AI/ML, large data, always-on fleets) should identify how consumption is observed so efficiency regressions are visible.
rules.remediationGuidance: Map consumption signals to governance.RequiredControls for AI/data/high-scale contexts.

rules.title: Resource retirement and disposal path
rules.description: Temporary environments, abandoned capacity, and retired data paths should have a disposal/retirement expectation.

rules.title: AI/accelerator efficiency screening when accelerators are in scope
rules.description: When GPUs/accelerators or generative AI are in scope, justify model size, inference frequency, batching, and always-on vs scheduled capacity without inventing emissions math.
rules.remediationGuidance: For AI/accelerator workloads, record model/inference efficiency rationale in metadata.ChangeDescription; flag missing evidence rather than fabricating carbon deltas.
